question: Which exact 3.1.32 function registers a character driver at /dev/canopus?
prototype_hypothesis: int register_driver(const char *path, const struct file_operations *fops, void *priv)
callsite_evidence: Three sibling functions share the inode lock/reserve/unlock shape: 0xc4f7c40 sets type 1, 0xc4e3804 type 2, 0xc4e38ce type 7.
A Mirage run registering with 0xc4e38ce made /dev/canopus visible to block/mtd discovery and open returned ENOSYS.
The type-1 variant is the character-driver registration; it also returns inode_reserve errors instead of discarding them.
control_flow_evidence: All three reserve an inode, write fops at +16 and private at +28, and differ only in the type nibble.
ownership_analysis: Caller-owned fops and private pointer; the inode is owned by the VFS.
unsafe_assumptions: The inode type constants come from decompiled stock registrations, not a header.
recommended_probe: Register /dev/canopus with 0xc4f7c40 and open it from the installer context.
